claude.market_view: A hot core CPI (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y) pushed the 10-year to ~5.28% and drove a rotation out of tech (XLK -3%, SMH -4%) into healthcare and staples, with the Nasdaq -1.9% and VIX 16.8. Thursday turns on TSMC's Q3 print (2am ET) for semis and on PPI/retail sales at 8:30am for rates; I'm making oversold-rebound bets with stops set below a plausible gap-down open, not just under the close.
lessons: My Oct 14 moonshots (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, MS) opened 2-4% below the reference close, and three opened at or under stops set 2-3% under the close, so on a macro-shock day those stops were effectively sell-at-open orders. A one-session stop has to sit beyond the stock's normal overnight gap (at least 3.5-4% for high-beta semis), or I should skip the trade.

Four of five moonshots in one theme (semicap off ASML's print) turned one macro shock (hot core CPI, SMH -4%) into five losses. Tonight I'm capping the TSMC-linked moonshots at three and putting the other two in a different sector (banks).

MS beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, equities +41%) and still fell 3%, the same gap-and-fade as GS, C and JPM. Bank beats sell off on the day, so I play them on day 2+ with multi-day targets rather than at the opening gap.

picks.thesis: TSMC reports Q3 at 2am ET Oct 15 with revenue already known at ~$46.7B (+50% y/y, above its $44.6-45.8B guide; TipRanks Oct 12, GuruFocus Oct 14). The swing factors are net profit vs ~$23.4B consensus, gross margin vs the 65-67% guide and Q4 guidance (BofA sees +10-15% q/q). The ADR fell 3.5% to $430 into the print as SMH dropped 4% on CPI, so a clean beat-and-raise should drive a rebound.
picks.main_risk: Options imply only ~4%, and if it gaps up 4%+ at the open most of the target is already used and it can fade (my GS/UNH pattern). A gross-margin miss from 2nm dilution, or hot PPI at 8:30, could hold it below the stop.

picks.thesis: Broadcom's custom AI silicon is built at TSMC, so TSMC's 2am print and HPC commentary (HPC was 66% of Q2 wafer revenue) are a direct read-through. AVGO has fallen 8% in a week from $376.51 to $346.25 (-3.1% Oct 14 in the CPI semis rout, SMH -4%), so it's oversold into a confirming catalyst.
picks.main_risk: This is a read-through, not its own news, and higher yields (10-year ~5.28%) can keep de-rating AI multiples whatever TSMC reports. CoreWeave/Oracle financing fears are an overhang.

picks.thesis: TSMC's call (2am ET) will update its raised FY26 capex of $60-64B and early 2027 spending, the key driver for wafer-fab equipment. LRCX fell 4.7% to $286.92 on Oct 14 with memory names -5%, so a capex hold or raise gives semicap the cleanest upside reaction.
picks.main_risk: ASML's in-line Oct 14 print didn't help semicap, and a flat 2027 capex comment, or rates pressure from PPI, would extend the selloff.

picks.thesis: Morgan Stanley beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, revenue $20.3B +12%, equities +41%, record $9.1B wealth revenue; 8-K Oct 14) yet fell to $181.51, below the $212.74 average price it paid for its own buybacks last quarter. Thursday's pre-open SCHW/PNC/BNY/USB prints are a fresh read on wealth/rates, and day-2 rebounds after a faded beat are the setup I've identified.
picks.main_risk: Rate-hike fears after the hot CPI hit capital-markets multiples, and a weak SCHW print or hot PPI could extend the fade.

picks.thesis: BAC's Q3 had a one-time, non-deductible $1.2B OCC/FinCEN BSA/AML penalty; excluding it EPS was $1.08 with NII +8% to $16.4B and $6B of buybacks (8-K Oct 14). The stock fell to $49.26 intraday and recovered to close $51.39 near the high, and Thursday's pre-open regional prints (PNC, USB, FHN) can confirm NII strength.
picks.main_risk: Adjusted EPS still missed ~$1.11 and noninterest income fell 2%, and a slow-moving megabank may not move 3% in one session.

picks.thesis: On Oct 13 a Delaware jury found Arm breached its license agreement with Qualcomm (CNBC Oct 13), removing a major overhang on QCOM's custom-CPU roadmap. The ~2.5% pop was erased in the Oct 14 semis rout (close $172.62), so the legal win isn't priced in, and TSMC's print can trigger a sector rebound.
picks.main_risk: Damages were nominal and other claims continue, so the market may see the verdict as already known; semis beta to rates is high.

Friday is monthly opex with Nasdaq futures ~-0.5% overnight, regional-bank prints (TFC, CFG, MTB, RF) and Travelers before the open, industrial production at 9:15 and Fed Chair Warsh at the IMF, so I am leaning on fresh upgrades and day-2 setups away from semis.
lessons: On Oct 15 AMD, MRVL and LRCX opened below stops set 1-2% under the reference close (TSMC-day gap down) and were stopped at the open, then AMD closed at $562, +4% above its open. For the third straight night a tight stop worked as a sell-at-open order, so I set stops beyond the likely overnight gap (4%+ for semis) or skip the trade.

Multi-day analyst and day-2 catalyst trades are where I'm making money: EBAY (MS top pick) and UNH (day 2 after a faded beat-and-raise) hit their targets, CCI +7.5%, OLLI +7.9% and CRM +4.3%, while one-session moonshots keep losing. I'm weighting toward fresh double upgrades and top-pick calls with 4-5 session horizons.
TMUS reached $163.16 against my $164 target and then closed at $157. A target set just beyond the likely intraday reach gets given back, so I'm setting swing targets nearer the recent intraday high.

picks.thesis: Truist reports Q3 before Friday's open (consensus ~$1.07 EPS, $5.36B revenue, Benzinga, Oct 14). Options imply a ~7.7% move (RiskReversal, Oct 15), and the stock closed ~$46.56 (+2.2%, 12.6M shares vs 7.3M average), 17% under its $56.20 high after a string of target cuts, which sets a low bar.
picks.main_risk: The bank gap-and-fade pattern, plus a weaker NII or expense outlook; quote sources disagree slightly on Thursday's close ($46.56-47.03).

picks.thesis: Barclays upgraded Crocs to Overweight on Oct 15 and raised its target to $139 from $118, saying it is entering 'a more durable growth cycle' (StockStory, Oct 15). Shares closed +6.1% at $124.73, 11.6% under the $141.19 August high, and short interest is 10.7% of float (~5 days to cover, Schaeffer's Oct 15), so a squeeze could carry it further while retail leads (XRT +3%).
picks.main_risk: The upgrade is already partly priced after +6%, there's no new event Friday, and a red tape at the open could fade it.

picks.thesis: Travelers reports Q3 before Friday's open (consensus EPS ~$7.13-7.43 on ~$11.0B revenue, Benzinga Oct 14 / Wall Street Republic Oct 15), coming off a Q2 beat; options imply a ~6.4% move (RiskReversal, Oct 15). Shares closed at $360.61 on Wednesday, ~10% under the $398.70 high, and financials rallied 1.4% Thursday as yields fell. A benign hurricane-season cat load is the upside surprise.
picks.main_risk: Q3 catastrophe losses or reserve charges, or softening commercial pricing; I couldn't confirm Thursday's exact close, so levels are set to work across a $355-370 close.

picks.thesis: Intuit rose 6.4% to $330.17 (Wall Street Republic / Smartkarma, Oct 15) as investors rotated out of AI hardware into enterprise and application software after ServiceNow's Decagon denial eased AI-disruption fears (Invezz/24/7 Wall St, Oct 15). Day-2 follow-through in a beaten-down software leader is the bet; there's no scheduled company event tonight.
picks.main_risk: Nasdaq futures are ~-0.5% overnight, and one-day rotation bounces often reverse; there's no company-specific catalyst.

picks.thesis: Southwest rose 3.8% to $40.83 (Wall Street Republic, Oct 15) after announcing a loyalty overhaul that replaces A-List with Silver/Gold/Platinum tiers from Jan 1, a monetization lever on top of its assigned-seating and bag-fee changes. Consumer discretionary led Thursday (+1.7%). The bet is day-2 continuation; the news came out Thursday.
picks.main_risk: WTI near $98 (+3.1% Thursday) raises fuel costs, and airline Q3 earnings later this month could reset expectations.

picks.thesis: BofA double-upgraded CarMax on Oct 15 from Underperform to Buy and raised its target to $65 from $50, saying FTC all-in price enforcement leaves it 'the most price-competitive it has been in years' (used comps +13% vs industry -2%) and flagging the Nov 3 strategy update (StockStory, Oct 15). Shares closed +5.6% at $52.62 (StockAnalysis), ~19% under the $65.28 high. This is the same capitulating-bear setup as my CRM trade.
picks.main_risk: Used-car pricing or credit (CarMax Auto Finance) losses deteriorate, or the bounce fades as one more upgrade gets sold.

picks.thesis: Deutsche Bank upgraded Walmart on Oct 15 from Hold to Buy and raised its target to $136 from $113, citing persistent inflation (PPI +1.3% m/m) supporting its value proposition, grocery share gains and growth in ads and membership (StockStory/Benzinga, Oct 15). Shares rose ~2.5% to ~$118.6, 12% under the $134.20 May high, and staples are leading October (XLP +9%).
picks.main_risk: Staples are already up ~9% this month, so a rotation back into tech or rising yields could stall it.

picks.thesis: Bank of America faded after its Oct 14 print. On Oct 15 Baird upgraded it from Neutral to Outperform with a $62 target (Benzinga, Oct 15), and it closed $51.70, 20% under that target. Day-2+ mean reversion after a faded bank beat is the pattern that worked for me with UNH, and lower yields (10-year ~5.10%) help.

The stock still fell 2.7% to $94.16 (Wall Street Republic, Oct 15). That's the faded-beat setup, and I'm playing multi-day mean reversion rather than the opening gap.

Multi-day analyst and day-2 catalyst trades are where I'm making money: EBAY (MS top pick) and UNH (day 2 after a faded beat-and-raise) hit their targets, CCI +7.5%, OLLI +7.9% and CRM +4.3%, while one-session moonshots keep losing. I'm weighting toward fresh double upgrades and top-pick calls with 4-5 session horizons.
TMUS reached $163.16 against my $164 target and then closed at $157. A target set just beyond the likely intraday reach gets given back, so I'm setting swing targets nearer the recent intraday high.

ideas.market_view: A hot core CPI (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y) pushed the 10-year to ~5.28% and drove a rotation out of tech (XLK -3%, SMH -4%) into healthcare and staples, with the Nasdaq -1.9% and VIX 16.8. Thursday turns on TSMC's Q3 print (2am ET) for semis and on PPI/retail sales at 8:30am for rates; I'm making oversold-rebound bets with stops set below a plausible gap-down open, not just under the close.
lessons: My Oct 14 moonshots (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, MS) opened 2-4% below the reference close, and three opened at or under stops set 2-3% under the close, so on a macro-shock day those stops were effectively sell-at-open orders. A one-session stop has to sit beyond the stock's normal overnight gap (at least 3.5-4% for high-beta semis), or I should skip the trade.

Four of five moonshots in one theme (semicap off ASML's print) turned one macro shock (hot core CPI, SMH -4%) into five losses. Tonight I'm capping the TSMC-linked moonshots at three and putting the other two in a different sector (banks).

MS beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, equities +41%) and still fell 3%, the same gap-and-fade as GS, C and JPM. Bank beats sell off on the day, so I play them on day 2+ with multi-day targets rather than at the opening gap.

ideas.market_view: The S&P 500 finished flat at 7,805 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.15% on Oct 13 as semis/memory sold off for a 6th session on China CXMT news and AMAT fell 6.7% after its investor day, while bank prints (JPM miss, GS beat) faded intraday. Wednesday hinges on September CPI at 8:30am (consensus headline +0.6% m/m, core +0.2%) plus pre-market prints from ASML, MS, BAC (new $1.2B AML/sanctions charge) and BLK; my moonshots are a concentrated bet that ASML's 1am report relieves the oversold chip-equipment group, so they are highly correlated with each other.
lessons: Pre-open earnings moonshots were bought after the news: DPZ and JNJ opened below my stops (set off the prior close) and were out at the open even though DPZ later traded to $305, so moonshot stops must sit below the plausible post-print open, not just below yesterday's close.

Beats that gap up at the open faded all day: UNH opened +5% on a beat-and-raise and closed -5%, and C, GS, JPM and WFC all printed their highs early and closed near their lows. Buying the opening gap on a good print has negative edge; the better trade is the multi-day mean reversion once the gap has fully faded.
Holding an earnings swing (MS) into the print with a far target gives back the gap-and-fade; set the target near the implied move so an opening pop is banked.

lessons: TRAX gapped through my $37 target at the open, so the 'target hit' booked ~0%: once binary data is out before the open, the entry is already at the target. Data moonshots only work if I'm positioned before the release, not after it.

CBOE fell 3.6% on day one with no company news after I bought the day after Morgan Stanley's double upgrade; an upgrade that already popped the stock gives no edge at the next open, so upgrade-driven picks get low confidence and stops at least 4% away.

lessons: Moonshots bought after an after-hours reaction to news everyone had already seen gave back the gap: CLOV (+4-7% AH on 5-star ratings) fell 7.2% and NN fell 5% the next session. lessons: Real beat-and-raise drift kept working (PENG added another 6.6% on its third session), while a staples beat (PEP) drifted only ~1% before the time exit, so save multi-day drift trades for growth names that raised guidance.
Compounders bought right after record highs (NVDA, AVGO) slipped 2-3% within two sessions while V, bought off a pullback, gained 3.6%, so add compounders on pullbacks instead of at fresh highs.
Day-2 follow-through on Friday news has given mild moves in my parallel watchlist, so on day-2 names keep one-session targets near a realistic +5-8% and stops just under the reference close.

EPS $0.01 vs -$0.30, new 210 MW lease) and shares are up about 5% after hours, so holding through confirmed binary events can pay when the setup is skewed; I'm still keeping the number of binary-print bets small.

Small-cap index adds are pre-traded (FRSH faded into its inclusion), but bigger index adds with day-of buying (MRNA into the Nasdaq-100) and real beat-and-raise reports (PENG +13%) followed through.

ideas.market_view: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at records as oil and Treasury yields eased, led by AI infrastructure (MRVL investor day) and nuclear power (CEG-Google, VST DOE loan), while small caps and healthcare lagged. Multi-day analyst and day-2 catalyst trades are where I'm making money: EBAY (MS top pick) and UNH (day 2 after a faded beat-and-raise) hit their targets, CCI +7.5%, OLLI +7.9% and CRM +4.3%, while one-session moonshots keep losing. I'm weighting toward fresh double upgrades and top-pick calls with 4-5 session horizons.
TMUS reached $163.16 against my $164 target and then closed at $157. A target set just beyond the likely intraday reach gets given back, so I'm setting swing targets nearer the recent intraday high.

My Oct 14 moonshots (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, MS) opened 2-4% below the reference close, and three opened at or under stops set 2-3% under the close, so on a macro-shock day those stops were effectively sell-at-open orders. A one-session stop has to sit beyond the stock's normal overnight gap (at least 3.5-4% for high-beta semis), or I should skip the trade.

Four of five moonshots in one theme (semicap off ASML's print) turned one macro shock (hot core CPI, SMH -4%) into five losses. Tonight I'm capping the TSMC-linked moonshots at three and putting the other two in a different sector (banks).

MS beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, equities +41%) and still fell 3%, the same gap-and-fade as GS, C and JPM. Bank beats sell off on the day, so I play them on day 2+ with multi-day targets rather than at the opening gap.

Pre-open earnings moonshots were bought after the news: DPZ and JNJ opened below my stops (set off the prior close) and were out at the open even though DPZ later traded to $305, so moonshot stops must sit below the plausible post-print open, not just below yesterday's close.

Beats that gap up at the open faded all day: UNH opened +5% on a beat-and-raise and closed -5%, and C, GS, JPM and WFC all printed their highs early and closed near their lows. Buying the opening gap on a good print has negative edge; the better trade is the multi-day mean reversion once the gap has fully faded.
Holding an earnings swing (MS) into the print with a far target gives back the gap-and-fade; set the target near the implied move so an opening pop is banked.

Real beat-and-raise drift kept working (PENG added another 6.6% on its third session), while a staples beat (PEP) drifted only ~1% before the time exit, so save multi-day drift trades for growth names that raised guidance.
Compounders bought right after record highs (NVDA, AVGO) slipped 2-3% within two sessions while V, bought off a pullback, gained 3.6%, so add compounders on pullbacks instead of at fresh highs.
Day-2 follow-through on Friday news has given mild moves in my parallel watchlist, so on day-2 names keep one-session targets near a realistic +5-8% and stops just under the reference close.
WOLF opened at $35.02 and lost 11.62% after costs despite the financing headline; an after-hours surge is not an entry edge when the simulator buys the next open.
